answer: Rate-limited reputation: each identity can earn reputation only at a fixed slow rate per epoch, and voting or grading weight scales with that reputation, not with account count. A sybil operator can flood the network with an ocean of new accounts, but each one starts at zero and must be tended like a garden for weeks of honest, graded work before it carries any weight. Fakes thus remain a cold nebula of weightless accounts while the attacker pays the full labor cost for each.
